bergamot: Bright, sparkling citrus with a slightly bitter green edge and a floral lift — the defining freshness in classic eau de colognes.
lemon: Sharp, zesty citrus with a clean sour snap — the freshest and most familiar citrus note in perfumery.
orange: Sweet, juicy citrus with a soft, sunny roundness — warmer and rounder than lemon.
blood-orange: Juicy orange with a deeper, berry-tinged sweetness and a faint tart bite.
grapefruit: Bitter-sparkling citrus with a pithy edge — crisp, energizing, and slightly green.
pink-grapefruit: A softer, sweeter take on grapefruit — juicy citrus with less of the bitter bite.
yuzu: Japanese citrus with a tart, aromatic punch — sharper and more complex than lemon, with green floral undertones.
mandarin-orange: Sweet, soft citrus with a candy-like juiciness — the gentlest and most delicate of the citrus fruits.
lime: Tart, green citrus with a sharp, almost salty bite — crisper and more astringent than lemon.
citron: Large Mediterranean citrus with a thick, aromatic peel — dry, zesty, and intensely fresh with a woody-citrus depth.
bitter-orange: Tart, dry citrus from the Seville orange — more aromatic and less sweet than sweet orange, with a marmalade-like edge.
neroli: The blossom of the bitter orange tree — fresh, green-white floral with a honeyed citrus brightness.
petitgrain: Distilled from bitter orange leaves and twigs — green, woody citrus with a dry, slightly bitter freshness.
clementine: Small sweet citrus with a soft, juicy, candy-like sweetness — gentle and sunny.
jasmine: Rich, heady white floral with a honeyed sweetness and a faint animalic depth — one of perfumery's most opulent flowers.
jasmine-sambac: A variety of jasmine with a greener, fresher character — sweet and luminous with a tea-like brightness.
rose: The classic floral — layered, honeyed petals with green freshness and a soft spiciness that varies by variety.
damask-rose: The rose of perfumery — deep, jammy petals with a rich honeyed-spicy warmth.
bulgarian-rose: Rose oil from the Valley of Roses — fresh, dewy petals with a bright, slightly lemony lift.
turkish-rose: Rose from Isparta — velvety, warm petals with a rich, slightly powdery depth.
tuberose: Intensely creamy white floral with a narcotic sweetness — rich, heady, and unmistakably lush.
gardenia: Creamy, buttery white floral with a green, almost mushroom-like freshness — sweet but never light.
lily-of-the-valley: Delicate green-white floral — dewy, fresh, and softly sweet, like tiny spring bells.
orange-blossom: The flower of the orange tree — sweet, honeyed white floral with a radiant, sunlit warmth.
ylang-ylang: Exotic, custardy floral with a banana-like sweetness — rich, balmy, and intensely tropical.
magnolia: Creamy, citrus-tinged floral — fresh lemony petals over a soft, milky sweetness.
peony: Soft, watery floral with a fresh, rose-like sweetness — light, airy, and delicately fruity.
freesia: Bright, peppery-sweet floral — crisp and cheerful with a subtle green snap.
iris: Cool, powdery floral with a violet-like softness — elegant, refined, and slightly rooty.
orris: The dried root of the iris — buttery, powdery, and violet-like with a smooth, cosmetic softness.
violet: Soft, powdery floral with a sweet, slightly green delicacy — gentle and nostalgic.
violet-leaf: Crisp green note with a cucumber-like freshness — cool, watery, and sharply green.
mimosa: Fluffy yellow blossom — soft, powdery, and honeyed with a delicate almond-like sweetness.
osmanthus: Tiny golden blossom with an apricot-like fruitiness — sweet, leathery-soft, and subtly tea-like.
lilac: Fresh, dewy spring floral — green, slightly powdery, with a clean sweet lift.
hyacinth: Intense green floral with a sharp, almost peppery freshness — vivid and spring-like.
narcissus: Rich, honeyed floral with a green, slightly animalic depth — heady and complex.
wisteria: Soft, lilac-like floral with a sweet, slightly powdery bloom — gentle and romantic.
orchid: Usually a perfumer's fantasy accord rather than a true flower — rendered as a soft, sweet, powdery floral.
lotus: Watery, translucent floral — cool, clean, and faintly sweet, like still pond water.
water-lily: Crisp aquatic floral — fresh, green, and clean with a delicate watery sweetness.
carnation: Spicy floral with a clove-like warmth — peppery, sweet, and richly aromatic.
heliotrope: Sweet, powdery floral with a distinct almond-cherry character — soft and comforting.
geranium: Green, rosy floral with a minty sharpness — fresh and aromatic with a rose-like heart.
saffron: Leathery, hay-like spice with a dry bitterness — warm, distinctive, and slightly medicinal.
cardamom: Sweet spice with a eucalyptus-like freshness — warm, aromatic, and gently camphorous.
cinnamon: Warm, sweet spice with a woody dryness — cozy and familiar with a gentle heat.
clove: Intense, numbing spice — warm, peppery, and medicinal with a deep sweetness.
nutmeg: Warm, sweet spice with a soft woody roundness — mellow and comforting.
pink-pepper: Bright, rosy spice with a sparkling freshness — peppery but sweet and fruity rather than hot.
black-pepper: Dry, sharp spice with a woody heat — crisp and biting without sweetness.
sichuan-pepper: Tingling citrus-spice with a numbing, electric freshness — brighter and more aromatic than black pepper.
ginger: Fresh, zesty spice with a lemony heat — sparkling and clean rather than heavy.
coriander: Warm, sweet spice with a nutty, slightly citrus character — soft and aromatic.
cumin: Earthy, warm spice with a musky, slightly sweaty depth — pungent and distinctly savory.
star-anise: Sweet licorice spice with a warm, glossy depth — richer and deeper than anise.
anise: Sweet, fresh licorice with a cool, herbal brightness.
pimento: Allspice — the warm blend of clove, cinnamon, and nutmeg notes found in a single berry.
galbanum: Intensely green resin with a sharp, earthy bite — the classic green note of traditional chypres.
tomato-leaf: Crisp, green, slightly bitter leaf — fresh and garden-like with a distinctive vegetal snap.
fig-leaf: Green, milky, coconut-tinged leaf — fresh and creamy with a soft tropical edge.
basil: Sweet-green herb with a peppery, anisic brightness — fresh and aromatic.
rosemary: Pungent, camphorous herb — clean, medicinal, and sharply green.
thyme: Warm, earthy herb with a dry, medicinal depth — savory and aromatic.
sage: Soft, camphorous herb with a cool, slightly bitter greenness.
mint: Cool, fresh herb with a sweet, icy lift — clean and bracing.
eucalyptus: Sharp, camphorous green with a medicinal coolness — intensely fresh and clearing.
juniper: Dry, gin-like berry with a piney, resinous crispness — clean and coniferous.
cypress: Dry, woody evergreen with a smoky, resinous depth — austere and green.
pine: Fresh, resinous conifer — crisp, turpentine-bright, and forest-clean.
absinthe: Bitter green liqueur herb — wormwood-sharp, anisic, and darkly aromatic.
tea: Dry, slightly smoky leaf with an elegant astringency — calm and refined.
green-tea: Fresh, grassy tea with a clean, dewy brightness — light and uplifting.
black-tea: Deep, malty tea with a smoky, leathery richness — warm and full-bodied.
fig: Creamy, milky fruit with a green, coconut-like softness — sweet but never sharp.
apple: Crisp, juicy fruit with a clean, watery freshness — bright and familiar.
pear: Soft, watery fruit with a delicate, dewy sweetness — gentle and fresh.
peach: Velvety, juicy fruit with a creamy, sun-warmed sweetness.
apricot: Soft, velvety fruit with a honeyed, slightly musky sweetness.
pineapple: Tart-tropical fruit with a juicy, sparkling sharpness.
mango: Lush tropical fruit — sweet, resinous, and richly juicy.
coconut: Creamy, milky tropical note with a soft, sun-warmed sweetness.
watermelon: Watery, crisp fruit with a light, airy sweetness — refreshing and clean.
melon: Soft, juicy fruit with a sweet, watery freshness — gentle and summery.
black-currant: Tart, dark berry with a green, sharp bite — juicy and vivid.
raspberry: Sweet-tart berry with a soft, jammy richness.
strawberry: Sweet, jammy berry with a soft, creamy ripeness.
cherry: Juicy stone fruit with a sweet-tart depth and an almond-like undertone.
plum: Dark, jammy fruit with a wine-like richness — sweet and velvety.
quince: Tart golden fruit with a floral, honeyed sharpness — crisp and aromatic.
pomegranate: Tart, juicy red fruit with a sparkling, wine-like freshness.
rhubarb: Tart, green stalk with a sharp, vegetal sourness — crisp and mouthwatering.
vanilla: Warm, sweet, and creamy — the classic gourmand note with a soft, balsamic depth.
tonka-bean: Warm, sweet bean with an almond-cherry character and a hay-like softness — like vanilla with extra depth.
honey: Rich, golden sweetness with a waxy, animalic warmth — lush and enveloping.
caramel: Burnt-sugar sweetness — warm, buttery, and deeply comforting.
chocolate: Rich, dark sweetness with a roasted, slightly bitter depth.
cacao: Raw chocolate — drier and more bitter than chocolate, with an earthy depth.
coffee: Dark, roasted bean with a bitter, smoky richness — bold and energizing.
almond: Soft, sweet nuttiness with a marzipan-like creaminess.
bitter-almond: Sharp, cherry-like nuttiness with a distinctive sweet-bitter snap.
pistachio: Creamy, buttery nut with a soft, milky sweetness.
hazelnut: Rich, buttery nut with a warm, roasted depth.
coumarin: The sweet hay-like molecule behind tonka — warm almond-vanilla sweetness with a tobacco-like softness.
brown-sugar: Deep, molasses-like sweetness — warmer and richer than white sugar.
toffee: Buttery, burnt-sugar sweetness with a creamy, chewy richness.
praline: Caramelized nut sweetness — roasted, buttery, and indulgent.
rum: Dark, boozy sweetness with a molasses warmth — rich and spirited.
sandalwood: Creamy, buttery wood with a soft, milky smoothness — warm, calm, and meditative.
cedar: Dry, pencil-shaving wood with a clean, aromatic crispness.
atlas-cedar: Cedar from Morocco — dry, camphorous wood with a warm, slightly sweet depth.
virginia-cedar: American cedar — softer and sweeter than Atlas, with a smooth, dry woodiness.
vetiver: Earthy, smoky grass root — dry, green, and grounding with a woody depth.
amyris: West Indian wood often called poor man's sandalwood — soft and creamy with a balsamic sweetness, milder than true sandalwood.
guaiac-wood: Smoky, rosy wood with a tar-like depth — warm, incense-like, and distinctive.
hinoki-wood: Japanese cypress — clean, lemony wood with a serene, temple-like calm.
papyrus: Dry, earthy reed with a dusty, parchment-like character — austere and green.
bamboo: Fresh, green, watery wood — clean and crisp with a dewy lightness.
oak: Dense, tannic wood with a dry, wine-barrel depth — sturdy and grounding.
amber: Warm, resinous glow — sweet, powdery, and enveloping, classically built from labdanum, benzoin, and vanilla.
labdanum: Dark, leathery resin with an ambery, animalic warmth — the backbone of classic amber accords.
benzoin: Sweet, vanilla-like resin with a warm, balsamic softness — cozy and smooth.
myrrh: Bitter, earthy resin with a dry, medicinal depth — ancient and contemplative.
frankincense: Bright, citrus-pine resin with a sacred, church-like smokiness — clean and uplifting.
olibanum: The resin also known as frankincense — lemony-pine brightness with a dry, mystical smoke.
opoponax: Sweet, balsamic resin with a warm, honeyed depth — softer and sweeter than myrrh.
elemi: Fresh, lemony resin with a green, peppery brightness — crisp and uplifting.
peru-balsam: Warm, vanilla-cinnamon balsam with a soft, powdery sweetness — rich and comforting.
oud: Rare agarwood resin — deep, animalic wood with smoky, leathery, honeyed complexity.
leather: Smoky, animalic tanning note — rich, warm, and darkly smooth.
suede: Softer than leather — velvety, powdery, and gently warm.
tobacco: Dry, honeyed leaf with a warm, slightly smoky sweetness — rich and comforting.
tobacco-leaf: The raw leaf — greener and drier than cured tobacco, with a hay-like warmth.
oakmoss: Damp, earthy lichen with a dark forest-floor depth — the soul of the classic chypre.
ambergris: Rare, waxy fixative with a salty, musky warmth — animalic yet soft, with a skin-like glow.
musk: Soft, skin-like warmth — clean, powdery, and quietly animalic.
white-musk: The clean modern musk — soft, laundry-fresh, and smooth with a gentle sweetness.
castoreum: Animalic leather note — smoky, tarry, and warmly musky.
aldehydes: Sparkling, soapy-waxy molecules — the fizzy lift in classic florals, like champagne bubbles.
calone: The marine molecule — watery melon and sea-spray freshness, the heart of aquatic scents.
iso-e-super: Velvety woody-amber molecule — smooth, cedar-like warmth with a subtle, skin-close radiance.
ambroxan: Dry, salty ambergris-like molecule — warm, mineral, and musky with a modern edge.
cashmeran: Musky-woody molecule with a warm, fuzzy softness — like cashmere rendered as scent.
hedione: Airy jasmine-like molecule — fresh, radiant, and transparent with a dewy lift.
smoke: Dry, charred woodiness — from campfire-soft to incense-dark, always atmospheric.
incense: Sacred resin smoke — frankincense and myrrh burning, mystical and meditative.
birch: Tar-like, leathery smoke — the dark, smoky backbone of classic leather scents.
sea-salt: Crisp mineral salinity — clean, ozonic, and bracing like ocean air.
seaweed: Briny, green marine note — salty and vegetal with a tidal freshness.
driftwood: Sun-bleached, salty wood — dry, mineral, and quietly marine.
